differences.text: `isOpen`/`onOpenChange` are `open` and the cancelable `tct-open-change` (with `tct-after-open-change`); `hasScrim` is `no-scrim`; `finalFocusRef` is `finalFocusElement` or `final-focus`; `snapPoints` is a property and a space or comma separated `snap-points` attribute. Inside a `tct-bottom-sheet-switcher` a sheet takes its `sheet-id` from the attribute, like upstream, and a sheet in a sheet's content is standalone.

WCAG 2.5.7: upstream's handle is decorative and the stops are reachable by dragging only. A sheet with snap points has a resizable handle: a labelled vertical slider (`aria-valuetext` is the visible share of the viewport) with Arrow Up/Down, Page Up/Down, Home, End, and Enter/Space to cycle; a tap on the handle (a press that never moves) also cycles, so every stop is reachable with a single pointer and no drag. A `tct-snap-change` event reports every user-driven change. The handle is at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8). A sheet without stops keeps the decorative handle: Escape, the scrim and your own controls are the ways to close it (a `no-scrim` sheet needs a close control of your own).

Geometry: the sheet is a native `<dialog>` that is a zero-height strip along the bottom edge, with the panel overflowing it upwards, so the layer stack's own "press outside" logic sees the backdrop as outside the dialog (upstream is a full-viewport dialog with a click check). Every stop is drawn with `translate`. Content below the fold at a lower stop stays reachable because the scrolling body gives up the resting offset as block-end margin and the sheet is pinned to its measured height: the swap happens when a slide down ends (and at once going up), so the visible geometry never changes. Upstream keeps a separate scroll-preservation inset; here a scroll position past the shorter scroll range can be clamped when a sheet that was scrolled to the end expands.

No drop shadow (D-013): a 1px rule on the three edges that face the scrim (block start and both inline edges) on the surface fill separates the sheet in dark mode too. The handle pill uses the emphasized border colour so it keeps 3:1 against the surface. The scrim is `--color-overlay`; forced colours drop it and draw the panel with `Canvas`/`CanvasText`.

Mobile keyboard: only a fully expanded `tall` sheet is accommodated (as upstream): it stays put, the body ends with a spacer as tall as the keyboard (measured with the visual viewport) and the focused text field is scrolled above it with a 48px clearance; starting a drag blurs the field. Upstream's iOS-specific focus hand-over (`preventScroll` on every route into a field, restoring a document scroll) is not ported: the visual viewport listeners run only while a field of the sheet has focus, and `interactive-widget=resizes-content` pages need none of it. Provisional until it is verified on iOS Safari.
Upstream's `BottomSheetEdgeTint` (an invisible fixed strip that colours the iOS Safari 26 toolbar) is kept as `.edge-tint` inside the shared dialog; it renders nothing visible.

provisional: Mobile keyboard handling on iOS Safari (BOTTOMSHEET-05) is verified in Chromium only.

differences.text: `onActiveSheetChange(null)` is the cancelable `tct-open-change` (`open: false`), after which the switcher clears `active-sheet` itself; the switcher is not a controlled component (D-006). The sheets talk to their switcher through a private context (a sheet provides `null` to its own content, so a sheet in a sheet is standalone) and receive their phase (`entering`, `active`, `covered`, `aligning`, `fading`, `exiting`, `hidden`) as an internal property.
The shared dialog is a zero-height strip like a standalone sheet's (BOTTOMSHEET-03), so the backdrop is outside it for the layer stack. A `no-scrim` flow opens it non-modally and takes no focus.
